display.title: Episode 284: The Rambam's Grave (Shiva Asar B'Tammuz)
display.summary_short: A Shiva Asar B'Tammuz show without music: why we ask 'Ad Masai', the life of the Rambam, and how a camel led his funeral caravan to his resting place in Teveria.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Shiva Asar B'Tammuz 5747, the first day of the Three Weeks, the show opens without the usual drums and singing. Uncle Yossi explains the chain from Asarah B'Teves to the breach of Yerushalayim's walls and the Churban on Tisha B'Av, and teaches that while we ask Hashem 'Ad Masai, how much longer?', Hashem waits for us to prepare for Moshiach through more Torah and mitzvos. He passes on the Rebbe's call for everyone to learn Rambam daily. Story time tells the Rambam's life: his flight from Cordova, years of wandering, a stormy voyage to Eretz Yisroel, and his settling in Egypt, where he wrote his great works. After he passes away, cities argue over where to bury him, and robbers attack the funeral caravan in the desert. Two brothers say the Shema in Studio 604 and tell how they share the Twelve Pesukim with friends. The story concludes: the robbers who approach the coffin fall down, they flee, and the camel walks on by itself to the place in Teveria where the Rambam is buried.
display.lesson: We ask Hashem 'how much longer?', but Hashem is also waiting for us: learning more Torah and doing more mitzvos prepares the world for Moshiach.
